---
title: "Trump tariffs v2.0 Update"
description: "The trade war is on: Canada gets a preferential 10% rate on energy given US reliance on Canadian crude, while Mexico still faces the full 25%."
date: "2025-02-02"
categories: [trade-wars]
---

With the tariffs now in effect, the picture has shifted: Mexico still faces a
flat 25% duty, but Canada gets a preferential structure — 10% on energy
imports and 25% on everything else — reflecting how dependent the US is on
Canadian crude oil. Under this modified approach, modelled Canadian export
losses improve from -23.9% to -20.4% in the no-retaliation scenario, though
the piece stresses the trade war still carries substantial welfare costs for
all sides if retaliation follows.

**Originally published on Substack**, February 2, 2025.
